title: How a Ductless Heat Pump Can Save You Money and Energy | Mitsubishi Electric HVAC US
summary: Mitsubishi Electric (vendor) article: ductless heat pumps combine heating and cooling, avoid duct losses, allow zoning; seal the envelope.

assertions.quote: Ductless heating and air conditioning systems can save 30-40 percent off the energy costs of a forced air system.

verdicts.note: Ductless systems avoid duct losses, which are large when ducts run through unconditioned space, but vendor savings figures are not independently measured.

For cooling, homes cooled only by mini-splits used about 194 kWh per season against an estimated 830-1,000 kWh for central AC (a TRM estimate, not a metered comparison); for heating they were not cheaper than a gas forced-air system.

assertions.quote: switching to a ductless heat pump system can kill two birds with one stone, bringing both cooling and heating in one system.
A heat pump is an energy-saving air conditioner that simply reverses the flow of refrigerant.
You can save a lot of money and energy by sending less heat into lesser-used areas of your home.

verdicts.note: Heating fewer rooms uses less energy, but the saving depends on occupants actually setting back unused zones.

Owners often heated or cooled only occupied rooms with the mini-split while the central system stayed low, which the evaluators say produces zonal savings not counted in their baselines; the effect was observed but not quantified.

assertions.quote: You need to make sure you have adequate insulation, and that all window, door and attic air leaks are sealed.
